title: Thin Cylinder Formula — Arch Stress

P.description: Hydrostatic pressure at the elevation = γw × h

R.description: Radius of arch ring at the elevation

applicability: First approximation for proportioning. Assumes uniform radial load, circular arch, pin-ended at abutments. Underestimates stress where cantilever action is significant. For initial sizing: t = P × R / σ_allow.
source: Classical mechanics, USBR Design of Arch Dams

title: Optimal Central Angle for Minimum Volume

2α_opt.description: Optimal total central angle of arch ring

applicability: Theoretical optimum for minimum concrete volume under uniform radial load. Practical range: 100–150°. Angles < 100° are too flat (high thrust, poor efficiency). Angles > 150° create unfavorable thrust direction at abutments.
source: USBR Design of Arch Dams, theoretical derivation

title: Arch Thrust at Abutment
equation: T = P × R / (2 × sin(α)) × (per unit height)

T.description: Thrust force per unit height at abutment

applicability: For circular arch under uniform radial load. Thrust is directed along the tangent to the arch at the abutment. Thrust direction relative to abutment rock surface is critical for sliding analysis.

title: Arch Ring — Crown Deflection (Elastic)

E.description: Modulus of elasticity of concrete (25–35 GPa)

I.description: Moment of inertia of arch ring = t³/12 (per unit height)

f(α).description: Function of half central angle — from structural tables

applicability: Used in trial load method to compute arch deflection for compatibility with cantilever deflection. Foundation flexibility adds additional deflection at abutments.

title: Cantilever Deflection at Crown
equation: δ_cant = (w × z⁴) / (8 × E × I_cant) (simplified — uniform load, fixed base)

δ_cant.description: Radial deflection of cantilever at the crown elevation

w.description: Cantilever portion of water load (distributed radial load per unit height)

z.description: Height of cantilever element above base

I_cant.description: Moment of inertia of cantilever cross-section

applicability: Simplified — actual cantilever analysis includes variable thickness, inclined upstream face, foundation flexibility. In trial load method, cantilever load is the residual after arch carries its share.

title: Thermal Stress in Arch Ring
equation: σ_thermal = E × α_T × ΔT / (1 - ν)  (restrained arch)

σ_thermal.description: Thermal stress (tension for cooling, compression for heating)

α_T.description: Coefficient of thermal expansion (9–12 × 10⁻⁶ /°C for concrete)

applicability: Arch dams are sensitive to temperature — a 10°C cooling below closure temperature can induce 2–4 MPa tension. Closure (grouting) temperature selected to minimize stress range over annual temperature cycle. Typical closure temperature = mean annual temperature of reservoir ± adjustment.

title: Abutment Sliding Stability — 3D Wedge Analysis

ΣN.description: Sum of forces normal to sliding surface (including weight, arch thrust component, uplift)

A_contact.description: Area of sliding surface in contact

ΣS.description: Sum of forces parallel to sliding surface (driving forces)

applicability: 3D wedge analysis on identified potential sliding planes (faults, joints, shear zones). Multiple sliding planes may form composite wedge. Direction of arch thrust relative to sliding surface is critical. FS requirements: ≥ 2.0 usual, ≥ 1.5 unusual, > 1.0 extreme (FERC).

title: Crest Length to Height Ratio
applicability: Key index for arch dam feasibility: L/H < 3: ideal for thin arch. L/H 3–5: thick arch or arch-gravity. L/H > 5–6: gravity dam usually more economical. Actual threshold depends on site geology and economics.

title: Base Pressure — Thick Arch (Combined Arch and Cantilever)

σ.description: Normal stress at a point on the cross-section

N.description: Axial thrust in the arch or cantilever

y.description: Distance from neutral axis to point of interest

applicability: For arch rings: N is the arch thrust, M is the arch bending moment (from non-uniform loading, fixed abutments). For cantilevers: N is the vertical weight, M is from the portion of hydrostatic load carried by cantilever action. Stresses checked at upstream face, downstream face, and abutment contacts.
source: General structural mechanics, USBR Trial Load Method

title: Foundation Modulus Ratio
applicability: Ef/Ec ratio strongly affects load distribution. Ef/Ec > 1: stiff foundation, more load carried by arches. Ef/Ec < 1: flexible foundation, more load to cantilevers, higher deflections. Ef/Ec < 0.25 generally problematic for arch dams — excessive deformation. Rock mass modulus typically 30–70% of intact rock modulus depending on jointing.
